tasks.gr7-adjectives-comparison-t1: Topic: Adjectives and degrees of comparison (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover attributive and predicative adjectives, the positive, comparative and superlative degrees, forming them (er/est, r/st after e, doubling the consonant, y to i, more/most with long adjectives), the irregular good-better-best, bad-worse-worst and many-more-most, using than and the, and the errors of double comparatives and superlatives for two things. Use South African English spelling and invented names. Ask Grade 7 learners to form and choose the correct degree with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-prefixes-suffixes-roots-t1: Topic: Prefixes, suffixes and roots (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover the root, prefixes (re again, pre before, sub under, inter between, anti against, un/dis/in/im/non not, mis wrongly), suffixes (ful, less, ness, ment, tion, able, ible, ly, er, or, ous), spelling changes (silent e, y to i, doubling) and the Latin and Greek roots port (carry), dict (say), scrib/script (write) and aud (hear). Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the parts and meanings with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-sentence-parts-clauses-t1: Topic: Sentence parts and clauses (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover subject and predicate, subject-verb agreement, a clause as a group of words with its own subject and verb, simple sentences, the main clause and the dependent clause, conjunctions that start dependent clauses (because, when, although, if, while, since, that), and phrases as groups of words without their own subject and verb. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the parts with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-multiple-meanings-t1: Topic: Words with more than one meaning (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover homophones (same sound, different spelling and meaning: their/there, to/too/two, write/right, sea/see), homonyms (same spelling and sound, unrelated meanings: bat, bank, bark, match), polysemy (related meanings, such as head), literal and figurative meaning, and riddles that use a word with two meanings. Ask Grade 7 learners to choose the correct word or meaning with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-spelling-dictionary-t1: Topic: Spelling patterns, rules and dictionary use (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover plurals (s, es, consonant plus y to ies, f/fe to ves, irregular), adding ing and ed (silent e, doubling the consonant, y to i), silent letters, South African English spelling (colour, favourite, centre; practise the verb and practice the noun), and a dictionary entry (headword, part of speech, meaning, example, guide words, alphabetical order). Ask Grade 7 learners to choose the correct spelling with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-active-passive-voice-t2: Topic: Active and passive voice (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover transitive and intransitive verbs (only transitive verbs can be passive), the passive with a form of be plus the past participle in the simple present, simple past and future, the present progressive passive (am, is or are being plus the past participle), and when the passive is useful (instructions, reports, an unknown doer). Use invented names and South African English spelling. Ask Grade 7 learners to recognise and form the passive and the active with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-prepositions-adverbs-t2: Topic: Prepositions and adverbs (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover prepositional phrases, fixed prepositions (afraid of, interested in, good at, depend on, listen to), forming adverbs (ly, y to i, well from good, fast, hard and late as adverbs), adverbs modifying verbs, adjectives and other adverbs, and the difference between hard and hardly and between late and lately. Ask Grade 7 learners to choose the correct preposition or adverb with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-direct-reported-speech-t2: Topic: Direct and reported speech (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover reported statements (the verb moves back one tense: am to was, can to could, will to would; pronouns and time words change), reported questions (no question mark, statement word order, asked if or whether), reported commands (told or asked plus to, not to) and the changes now to then, tomorrow to the next day, yesterday to the day before, this to that, here to there. State the rule in the question where it is needed so that exactly one option is correct. Use invented names.
tasks.gr7-apostrophe-hyphen-quotation-t2: Topic: Apostrophe, hyphen and quotation marks (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover the apostrophe of possession (girl's, girls', children's), its for belonging and it's for it is, contractions, the hyphen in numbers, compound adjectives before a noun, some prefixes and word division between syllables, and quotation marks with the end punctuation inside the closing marks. Ask Grade 7 learners to choose the correctly punctuated version with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-clauses-t3: Topic: Noun, adjectival, adverbial and relative clauses (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover the three kinds of dependent clause (a noun clause does the work of a noun and is a subject or object, an adjectival or relative clause describes a noun, an adverbial clause tells when, why, where or how), relative pronouns (who for people, whose for belonging, whom for people as the object, which for things) and adverbial conjunctions (when, after, before, because, since, although, if, where). Do not use that as a relative pronoun option. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the kind of clause and choose the relative pronoun with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-pronouns-t3: Topic: Pronouns (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover personal pronouns (subject I, he, she, we, they and object me, him, her, us, them), possessive pronouns (mine, yours, his, hers, ours, theirs) against possessive adjectives, reflexive pronouns (myself, himself, themselves), demonstrative, interrogative, indefinite and relative pronouns, and agreement of a pronoun with its noun. Ask Grade 7 learners to choose the correct pronoun with exactly one correct option and no sentence where another option is also grammatical.
tasks.gr7-verbs-gerunds-t4: Topic: Verbs: auxiliary, finite and non-finite, and gerunds (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover the finite verb (shows tense and agrees with its subject), non-finite forms (infinitive, present participle, past participle), auxiliary verbs (be, have, do, will, can, may, must), irregular participles (broken, sung, eaten, run) and the gerund (an ing form that works as a noun) against the present participle. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify the form with exactly one correct option.
tasks.gr7-bias-emotive-language-t4: Topic: Bias, stereotypes and emotive language (Grade 7 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover bias (a one-sided view), prejudice (an unfair opinion without the facts), stereotypes (a fixed oversimplified idea about a group), emotive language (words that make the reader feel something), manipulative language and rhetorical questions, and how to check a text (who wrote it, what is left out). Use invented examples and no real group, person or product. Ask Grade 7 learners to identify these with exactly one correct option.
